business_problem: HK01's PHP/MySQL monolith struggled to handle 10 billion annual page views, rapidly changing content models, Chinese-language search requirements, and the operational burden of scaling a global media platform without dedicated DBA capacity.
solution_summary: HK01 rebuilt its high-traffic media platform on MongoDB Atlas and MongoDB Atlas Search after a PHP/MySQL monolith could no longer keep up with 10 billion annual page views, rapidly changing content models, and real-time engagement requirements. Rather than perform a risky lift-and-shift, the company introduced new services as independently scalable microservices on Atlas while legacy components continued running beside them. The document model lets teams add metadata fields, engagement metrics, FAQs, maps, and tables without disruptive schema migrations, and Atlas's managed reliability reduces the need for scarce DBA effort. Atlas Search is being rolled in to support editorial discovery and reader-facing content retrieval, giving HK01 tunable analyzers and tokenization strategies that are especially important for Chinese-language relevance as the company expands into Mainland China.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores HK01's evolving content and engagement data in a microservices architecture built for high traffic.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Provides tunable full-text search for editorial discovery and reader-facing content retrieval.

data_flow: Content and engagement data is written into MongoDB Atlas by newly built microservices while legacy components continue to run during the phased migration. Atlas Search indexes that content so editors and readers can retrieve relevant Chinese-language results without a separate search stack.
business_outcome: HK01 gained zero MongoDB-cluster downtime, faster feature delivery without schema migrations, and a search stack that can improve Chinese-language relevance as the platform expands beyond Hong Kong.
